title: Pjotr Sillekens (biotech founder) — 'They drift because caring was never the mechanism. Intentions decay. Structures persist.'
summary: Pjotr Sillekens — biotech founder — publishes a substantive mid-read reflection applying Incorruptible's structural argument to his own live biotech data-stewardship commitments: the fair question customers can ask isn't whether we mean it, but what we've committed to that would survive us even if we don't.
blockquote: I'm reading Incorruptible by Eric Ries. His argument is uncomfortable in a useful way: companies don't drift because people stop caring. They drift because caring was never the mechanism. Intentions decay. Structures persist. So the fair question a customer can ask us isn't whether we mean it. It's what we've committed to that would survive us even if we don't mean it.
